1. Market Overview & Long-Term Price Trend

Gold compounded at 12.38% annually from $273.90 on 30 Aug 2000 to $5,377.30 on 03 Mar 2026. The price path is strongly regime-dependent: long bull phases are interrupted by multi-year drawdowns rather than smooth mean reversion.

The largest closing-price drawdown was -44.36%, running from the prior peak on 22 Aug 2011 to trough on 17 Dec 2015. That drawdown is central for portfolio construction because it shows gold can experience equity-like peak-to-trough losses even while preserving positive long-run convexity to macro stress.

Volatility is clustered and asymmetric across regimes. Crisis-vol days represent the top decile of 63D realized volatility, while low-vol periods sit below the 33rd percentile. Comparing regime returns with realized volatility provides a practical stress map: high realized volatility does not simply mean negative returns, but it materially widens expected daily P&L dispersion and drawdown risk.

3. Seasonal & Calendar-Based Patterns

Monthly averages show the highest mean daily log return in January and the weakest in June. However, the cross-month ANOVA p-value is 0.650 and Kruskal-Wallis p-value is 0.480, so the evidence for stable month-to-month differences should be treated as weak and likely noisy at conventional thresholds.

Day-of-week differences are similarly tested rather than inferred visually. The weekday ANOVA p-value is 0.551 and Kruskal-Wallis p-value is 0.254. Any calendar tilt should therefore be sized as a secondary input, not a standalone trading signal.

4. Return Distribution & Tail Risk

-0.47Daily log-return skewness
7.02Excess kurtosis
-3.05%Historical 1% daily VaR
-4.17%Historical 1% expected shortfall

Daily returns are not well-described by a thin-tailed normal distribution. Excess kurtosis of 7.02 indicates fat tails, while the historical left-tail risk is substantial: 5% daily VaR is -1.75% and 1% daily VaR is -3.05%. The worst daily return was -11.37% on 30 Jan 2026; the best daily return was 9.03% on 17 Sep 2008.

Absolute daily moves greater than 2% occurred on 6.8% of trading days and moves greater than 3% occurred on 2.0%. The 2% tail frequency is approximately 0.9× the frequency implied by a same-volatility normal model, reinforcing the need for stress-aware sizing.

5. Momentum Dynamics & Liquidity Behavior

72.7%Share of post-200D-valid days above 200D MA
27.1%Annualized return when above 200D MA
-27.8%Annualized return when below 200D MA
-0.03Post-2003 volume / |return| correlation

The latest close is above the 200-day moving average. Historically, returns when the close is above the 200D average annualized to 27.1%, versus -27.8% when below. The 50D/200D trend filter is also directionally informative: annualized return during 50D>200D regimes was 14.0%, compared with 7.2% when 50D≤200D.

Volume interpretation is limited before 2004 because the source brief flags zero/low early volume as unreliable. Using post-2003 data, volume is positively associated with absolute return magnitude: correlation between volume and |daily log return| is -0.03, while correlation with signed return is -0.02. This supports treating volume primarily as a participation/stress indicator rather than a directional signal.

6. Key Takeaways & Forward-Looking Considerations

  • Strategic allocation: the full-sample CAGR of 12.38% with annualized volatility of 17.69% gives gold a Sharpe-like ratio of 0.70; allocation sizing should reflect both positive long-run trend and deep drawdown capacity.
  • Risk management: volatility regimes are persistent enough to be operational. The latest 63D realized volatility is 36.5%, classified as Crisis-vol; risk budgets should adapt when the regime crosses high/crisis thresholds.
  • Tail risk: fat tails and 1% expected shortfall of -4.17% argue for stress tests beyond Gaussian VaR, especially during crisis-vol clusters.
  • Seasonality: monthly and weekday effects are smaller than trend/volatility effects and require statistical humility; use them only as weak tilts unless revalidated out-of-sample.
  • Momentum overlay: 200D and 50D/200D filters separate materially different return states in this dataset and can support tactical risk scaling.
  • Liquidity context: high volume aligns more with larger absolute moves than direction, useful for identifying crowded stress periods and execution-risk windows.

Current context from the dataset: trailing 252-trading-day return is 84.8%, trailing 252D realized volatility is 26.1%, and 2026 year-to-date return through 03 Mar 2026 is 24.6%. These should be read as descriptive data points, not forecasts.
